_comment: Vision 1.0 perception configuration (§50, §53). JSON so the shipped artefact loads on an
interpreter without PyYAML; .yaml is accepted when PyYAML is present.
The score thresholds and the §16 dedup thresholds are COMMISSION on purpose: nobody has
commissioned them on this station. validate(production=True) therefore refuses to start
for EVERY profile, offline_replay included - and validate(production=False), the mode
replays and acceptance tests use, reports them as work items instead of silently running.
Filling them in from a demo script's numbers is the drift §3.5 documents: the retired
pipeline's 'confidence' meant something else entirely.
profiles: person_detect (§6's baseline; the .rpk is not installed here),
person_detect_available (a post-processed COCO detector that IS installed, so §9.2's
oracle and the real adapter can be exercised today), offline_replay (mock adapter).
manifest_path is resolved by perception.model.adapter.resolve_artifact(): package
directory first, then next to this file, then the working directory - because a relative

manifest_path is resolved by perception.model.adapter.resolve_artifact(): the perception package directory first, then the Firmware root, then next to this file, then the working directory - because a relative path resolved against whatever directory systemd launched from is a silent wrong-file bug.
Bake-off profiles (§7/Vision-6): person_detect_available (ssd-mobilenetv2 fpnlite 320, 26 Hz),
bakeoff_nanodet416 (nanodet+ 416, 23 Hz), bakeoff_efficientdet320 (efficientdet-lite0, 23 Hz).
All three name an artefact that is installed, and each manifest's sha256, license and rate
were measured from the .rpk rather than written by hand; their score thresholds stay
COMMISSION, so `--production` still refuses them until the numbers are commissioned (§50).
Run `python -m perception.tools.bakeoff --recording REC` to compare them on one recording.
camera.width/height = 1920x1080 so the published TrackSet pixel geometry matches the
calibrated camera_intrinsics (calibration/camera_intrinsics.yaml is valid ONLY for the
1920x1080 tracker frame). If visiond publishes a different size, controld's aim-point check
(frame.width != intr.width) forces aim_point_valid=false and the turret never moves. The
IMX500's
on-sensor network runs on its own fixed crop regardless; this is the size §14
maps boxes into, and it is the size a 320x320 main stream turned out not to
deliver frames at (measured: configured fine, never a frame — the sensor has no
3xx-width main mode on this rp1-cfe/pisp stack).
selection.policy = AUTO_SELECT_SINGLE is the core feature (the turret auto-
selects the one person in view and follows it). auto_select_min_* are PROVISIONAL
values from the measured person detections (~0.9) vs clutter (<0.3); they are not
claimed §50-commissioned — recompute from a real person recording before a
production run, or the auto-select dwell cannot be trusted.
tracking thresholds are COMMISSION in the shipped file; the values set here are
PROVISIONAL (person ~0.9, clutter <0.3, the tracker's nominal bands). They close the
loop so the turret can track, but §50 still needs a real calibration recording before
a production run.
tracking/auto-select thresholds are set from the MEASURED person score (0.27-0.32 on
this sensor): selectable 0.30, auto_select_min_detector_score 0.27, etc. A floor above
0.32 excluded every actual person — this is the calibration fact commissioning exists to
surface. Recompute from a real labelled recording before a production run.
§16 dedup commissioned (nms_iou 0.45, containment_ratio 0.85, center_distance_norm 0.05):
without it the duplicate resolver declines, the 2:1 tensor cadence fragments the person
into 4-5 overlapping CONFIRMED tracks, and auto-select never sees a single candidate.
